output.name: Hunal
output.myth: Hunal was a ram of the north cliffs, and he loved one goat more than grass. In spring she ran out along a sea-stack, and Hunal ran after her, because a ram does not let a goat go alone. Tavo came up under them with a laugh and a gust, and the ram went off the edge, horns out ahead. Ennu the Kite-Wright says the horns caught in the cloud and held him there. So he stands on the wave-tops now, in the Unflown, horns up in the weather, hooves in the foam. Tanhá, the Gale's Tooth, sits sixteen degrees west of him, where Tavo once bit a salt-stiff kite-line. Twelve degrees north, the grey boatman of Varo watches. He takes shell coins from the drowned, and a ram has none to give him, so he only watches. The goat went home, which is the only part anyone likes. When you climb, do not follow your animals past the last rope. Hesk keeps count of who went over, and she has not finished counting that ram.
output.finding: Sailors far south find Hunal by starting at Varo, the Unpaid Crossing, and going about 12°, a little over a fist, straight south to where the ram's horns stand up in the foam.
